findings.text: The real 10 um Allen Nissl agrees with the 25 um stain the layers were derived from (r = 0.98), and the derived pyramidal layers sit on its dense band: mean 185 in CA1 sp against a field median of 53, 219 against 63 in CA3.

Four MouseLight tracings from different mice touch where they are registered: LEC AA1047 to granule cell AA0573 to CA3 AA0307 to CA1, found by surveying 656 registered hippocampal and entorhinal tracings (tools/seahorse/survey.py). The rides run on them.
MouseLight AA0621 touches CA3 AA0307 more closely (11 um) but 92% of its dendrites lie in the corpus callosum, not CA1; AA0306 (94% in CA1 strata) is used, moved 53 um.

The SEU-ALLEN entorhinal tracings on NeuroMorpho (Peng archive, 321 layer II/III cells) have dendrites only, despite their metadata; no public registered MEC layer II axon exists, so the medial perforant path is drawn along its atlas route.

The LEC cell AA1047 puts more of its axon in the derived middle third (MML) than the outer third; either the thirds (by depth) sit off the real lateral/medial boundary here, or this cell is near the LEC/MEC border (its dendrites reach MEC layer I).

NeuroMorpho lists MouseLight AA0998 as a dentate granule cell, but its axon is 186 mm long and stays in the molecular layer; real MouseLight granule cells have 3-5 mm axons through the hilus into CA3. AA0998 is not used.
MouseLight source files are (ML, DV, AP); SEU-ALLEN (Peng) files are (AP, DV, ML). Found by checking which order puts each soma in the region its authors named.
MouseLight AA0960, listed as CA1, has its soma in CA3 by the CCFv3 annotation (near the border); AA0959 (soma in CA1 sp) is used instead.

No mouse or rat mossy-cell tracing is on NeuroMorpho.Org (searched 2026-11-20), and none of the 19 registered hilar cells surveyed has a mossy-cell axon (mostly to the inner molecular layer); the mossy cell is drawn from published descriptions.
CCFv3 does not annotate CA strata or the thirds of the molecular layer; Seahorse derives them (see each layer), and the Nissl test above is how they are checked.

method:
Seahorse auto cross-check: test what the schematic claims against data.

    python tools/seahorse/crosscheck.py      -> web/seahorse/checks.json

Three kinds of test, each with a verdict the tab shows beside the claim:

  Allen connectivity   for a region-level connection A -> B: every Allen
                       Mouse Connectivity experiment whose primary injection
                       is in A; projection density in B (both hemispheres)
                       against the same experiments' density in cerebellum
                       (a structure none of these project to). supported if
                       the median is >= 0.002 and >= 5x the control.
  tracings             for a cell-level connection: the share of the
                       exemplar's axon (or dendrite) length in the layers the
                       claim names. 'evidence' when the tracing was registered
                       to CCF by its authors; 'placement' when the cell was
                       traced in a slice and placed here by fit -- then it only
                       says the placement is sane.
  laminae vs Nissl     each derived layer's mean Nissl density: granule and
                       pyramidal layers must be denser than their neighbors.

Plus findings: things the checks turned up about the sources themselves.

ca3 axon meets ca1 in ca1so (Schaffer collaterals: radiatum or oriens). Gap 53.4 um where traced, closed by moving ca1 53.4 um.
